observation: Live guidance is unavailable, but the interface does not show that Coach must first be activated.
The prerequisite for receiving live Coach guidance is not visible near the requested action.
The user cannot determine why live guidance is not being produced or what must be enabled.
The Bot switch and Stop button appear to control overlapping functions.
After using the switch or Stop button, the interface does not provide sufficiently clear status feedback.
It is unclear whether Stop ends the Bot process or disables the selected strategy mode.
Drive now and Plan and review are presented with insufficient visual distinction.
The two Coach modes are easy to confuse when moving between live and retrospective use.
The interface does not make the purpose of the two Coach views immediately recognisable.
Queue is a technical term and its effect is not clear to an end user.
The Commentary control uses implementation-oriented language instead of task-oriented language.
Users may not understand what content is being queued or when it will be played.
The interface exposes the HTTP 409 status code without a user-oriented explanation.
The error message does not clearly explain the cause or the recovery action.
The technical code is visible, although the failed operation can still be retried.
The continuously scrolling process log makes the current operational state difficult to locate.
Developer-oriented log output dominates the interface and there is no concise status such as Running.
Users must inspect multiple log lines to infer whether the process is active.
Toggle descriptions use inconsistent text lengths across modules.
Similar toggle controls do not use a consistent labelling pattern.
Uneven explanatory text creates a minor consistency and scanning problem.
